BUS.G12.T2.MGMTLEAD.A1.title: Management & leadership
BUS.G12.T2.MGMTLEAD.A1.description: Differentiating between management and leadership styles and approaches: the difference between leadership and management, leadership styles (democratic, autocratic, laissez-faire), theories of management and leadership (situational, transactional, transformational), and the role of personal attitude in success and leadership.
BUS.G12.T2.MGMTLEAD.A1.strand: T2 — CSR, human rights, teams, sector & environment, leadership & quality
BUS.G12.T2.MGMTLEAD.A1.recovery_strategy: Management = planning, organising and controlling the work. Leadership = inspiring and influencing people toward a vision. Autocratic leaders decide alone; democratic leaders involve the team; laissez-faire leaders are hands-off.

questions.question: What is the main difference between management and leadership?
options: Management organises the work; leadership inspires and guides people
They are exactly the same thing
questions.expected: Management organises the work; leadership inspires and guides people
questions.memo: Management is about planning, organising and controlling tasks; leadership is about inspiring and influencing people toward a vision.

questions.question: An autocratic leader mainly:
options: Makes decisions alone and tells the team what to do
questions.expected: Makes decisions alone and tells the team what to do
questions.memo: An autocratic leader keeps decision-making to themselves and directs the team.

questions.question: A _________ leader involves the team in making decisions.
questions.expected: democratic
questions.memo: A democratic leader consults the team and involves them in decisions.

questions.question: True or false: Leadership is about inspiring and influencing people towards a vision.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: Leadership focuses on inspiring, motivating and influencing people to pursue a shared vision.

questions.question: A laissez-faire leadership style is best described as:
options: Hands-off, leaving staff to make their own decisions
questions.expected: Hands-off, leaving staff to make their own decisions
questions.memo: Laissez-faire leaders take a hands-off approach, giving staff freedom to decide how to do their work.

questions.question: _________ leadership inspires major change and motivates people beyond their normal expectations.
questions.expected: Transformational
questions.memo: Transformational leadership inspires people with a vision and motivates them to achieve more than expected.

questions.question: Sort each activity into management or leadership.

items.text: Inspiring the team with a vision
Motivating staff to give their best

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Scheduling, budgeting and organising are management tasks; inspiring, motivating and influencing are leadership.

questions.question: In which situation is an autocratic style often most useful?
options: An urgent crisis where fast, clear decisions are needed
questions.expected: An urgent crisis where fast, clear decisions are needed
questions.memo: Autocratic leadership suits crises where quick, decisive direction matters more than wide consultation.

questions.question: Read both leaders, then decide which each statement matches.

source_a.text: I make the decisions and expect my team to carry them out without debate. It is faster this way.

source_b.text: I gather my team's views and we decide together. People are more committed when they have a say.

statements.text: Refuses to make any decision ever

questions.expected: s1=a_only, s2=b_only, s3=both, s4=neither
questions.memo: Leader A decides alone (autocratic); Leader B involves the team (democratic). Both lead; neither refuses all decisions.

questions.question: _________ leadership adapts its style to fit the situation and the people involved.
questions.expected: Situational
questions.memo: Situational leadership changes its approach depending on the task, the team and the circumstances.

questions.question: Transactional leadership mainly motivates people through:
options: Rewards for good performance and consequences for poor performance
questions.expected: Rewards for good performance and consequences for poor performance
questions.memo: Transactional leadership works through exchanges — rewarding good performance and correcting poor performance.

questions.question: True or false: A positive personal attitude supports good leadership.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: A leader's positive attitude influences the team's morale and is linked to success in leadership.

questions.question: Sort each description under the leadership style it fits.

items.text: The leader decides alone and directs the team
The leader consults the team before deciding
The leader lets staff decide for themselves
Strict control with little input from staff

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Deciding alone = autocratic; consulting the team = democratic; hands-off = laissez-faire.

questions.question: What is the difference between transactional and transformational leadership?
options: Transactional uses rewards and rules; transformational inspires change through a vision
Transactional avoids all targets; transformational sets none
questions.expected: Transactional uses rewards and rules; transformational inspires change through a vision
questions.memo: Transactional leadership runs on rewards and consequences; transformational leadership inspires people to embrace change and a shared vision.

questions.question: In which situation does a democratic style usually work well?
options: When team input is valuable and there is time to consult
When a decision is needed in seconds during a crisis
When no one in the team has any knowledge
When the leader wants to avoid all input
questions.expected: When team input is valuable and there is time to consult
questions.memo: Democratic leadership suits situations where the team's knowledge adds value and there is time to involve them.

questions.question: Management mainly focuses on planning, organising and _________.
questions.expected: controlling
questions.memo: The management tasks are planning, organising, leading/activating and controlling the work.

questions.question: Read two managers handling a sudden safety emergency, then decide which each statement matches.

source_a.text: During the gas leak I gave clear, direct orders immediately and everyone followed them. There was no time for discussion.

source_b.text: For our new product strategy I held workshops, gathered ideas from the whole team and we shaped the plan together.

statements.text: Used an autocratic style suited to a crisis
Used a democratic style suited to a creative task
Chose a style to fit the situation

questions.expected: s1=a_only, s2=b_only, s3=both, s4=neither
questions.memo: Manager A was autocratic in a crisis; Manager B democratic for a creative task. Both matched their style to the situation; neither failed to decide.

questions.question: A manager keeps every decision to themselves even for creative, long-term projects, and staff feel unmotivated. How is this best evaluated?
options: The autocratic style is poorly matched here; a more democratic style would likely raise motivation
Autocratic is always the best style for everything
The staff are simply wrong to feel demotivated
questions.expected: The autocratic style is poorly matched here; a more democratic style would likely raise motivation
questions.memo: Style should fit the situation; for creative, long-term work, involving the team (democratic) usually lifts motivation more than strict autocratic control.

questions.question: Why is matching leadership style to the situation important?
options: Different situations call for different approaches, and the right style improves results and morale
One fixed style is always best in every case
Style has no effect on a team
Leaders should change style at random
questions.expected: Different situations call for different approaches, and the right style improves results and morale
questions.memo: Situational leadership recognises that the best style depends on the task and people; matching them improves both results and morale.

questions.question: How do strong management and strong leadership together benefit a business?
options: Management keeps work organised and controlled, while leadership inspires people towards the vision
Only one is ever needed at a time
questions.expected: Management keeps work organised and controlled, while leadership inspires people towards the vision
questions.memo: A business needs both: management to organise and control the work, and leadership to inspire and guide people towards its goals.
